overview: Hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan spoke with Medford for Palestine organizers Josh Ekhart-Lee and Micah Kesselman about the successful passage of the city's Values Aligned Local Investments Ordinance after a City Council override of a mayoral veto. The discussion also addressed state-level pension divestment legislation, school curriculum advocacy, and local community building.

items.title: Introductions and Local Dining Favorites
items.summary: Hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan introduced Medford for Palestine organizers Josh Ekhart-Lee and Micah Kesselman, who shared their backgrounds and favorite local restaurants.

items.title: Update on the Values Aligned Local Investments Ordinance
items.summary: The guests explained that after the Medford City Council initially passed the local investment ordinance, Mayor Brianna Longo-Cohen vetoed the measure, which the council subsequently overrode in mid-November.

items.title: Implementation and Financial Impact of Divestment
items.summary: The organizers detailed how the ordinance proscribes investments in specific high-harm industries like Lockheed Martin and Chevron using ESG indices, with an implementation deadline set for December 31, 2025.

items.title: State-Level Pension Divestment Legislation
items.summary: Josh Ekhart-Lee and Micah Kesselman outlined state-level bills H-2984 and H-3001/S-1399, explaining that state authority is required to allow local retirement boards to divest public employee pensions.

items.title: Antisemitism Committee Recommendations in Schools
items.summary: Micah Kesselman raised concerns about recommendations to implement the IHRA definition of antisemitism in schools, warning that it conflates criticism of Israel with antisemitism, and urged residents to contact state representatives.

items.title: Community Action and Wrap-Up
items.summary: The guests provided resources for state legislative advocacy and encouraged listeners to connect with local mutual aid and neighborhood groups in Medford.
